topology: 2 nodes x 4 H100, 8 MPI ranks, 7 PP + 1 PME, OpenMPI 4.1.5 over UCX 1.15 (HPC-X 2.16) over NDR InfiniBand
why: GROMACS is the cleanest available instance of claim (3): one environment variable, GMX_DISABLE_DIRECT_GPU_COMM, switches halo exchange and PME-PP exchange between staging through host memory and handing device pointers straight to MPI. The application's own documentation asserts this is faster; nobody here has ever seen the switch in a trace. It also has an unusually derivable topology: with -npme 1 the PP/PME split and the DD grid are both forced by the command line (7 is prime, so the only DD grid is 7x1x1), so the halo partner set and the PME fan-in are oracles that name no identifier the run produced.
workload_note: Every number above is a command-line input or a tpr header field, not an observation of a capture. `ranks`, `npp`, `npme`, `dd_*`, `nsteps`, `nstlist` come from the mdrun invocation in job.sbatch. `natoms` is offset 72 of benchRIB.tpr (big-endian uint32 = 2136412), which matches the figure the Max Planck benchmark set publishes for benchRIB; it is read from the input file, never from md.log and never from the capture. `gpudirect` is the knob, and it is the only value that differs between the two captures — it is what lets one assertion file be the specification for both runs.

oracle_derivation.pme_rank_of_pp_rank: src/gromacs/domdec/domdec.cpp:540 ddindex2pmeindex() = (ddCellIndex*npme + npme/2)/npp, and :623 dd_simnode2pmenode() pmeRanks.empty() branch = numPPRanks + ddindex2pmeindex(sim_nodeid). With -ddorder pp_pme and npme=1 this is 7 for every PP rank 0..6. Each PP rank sends coordinates to, and receives forces from, exactly that one rank (src/gromacs/ewald/pme_pp.cpp:296 MPI_Isend(x.data(), n*sizeof(rvec), ..., dd->pme_nodeid) on the staged path, :256 of pme_pp_comm_gpu_impl_gpu.cpp MPI_Isend(sendptr_x, sendSize*DIM, MPI_FLOAT, pmeRank_) on the direct path).
oracle_derivation.dd_grid: npp = 7 is prime, so nx*ny*nz = 7 admits only a permutation of 7x1x1, and GROMACS decomposes x first. -dd 7 1 1 states it explicitly so the run cannot silently choose otherwise.
oracle_derivation.halo_partners: A 1-D DD grid of 7 cells is periodic, so cell x exchanges halo data only with cells (x+1) mod 7 and (x-1) mod 7. GROMACS stages halo exchange one dimension at a time (src/gromacs/domdec/gpuhaloexchange_impl_gpu.cpp communicateHaloData, src/gromacs/domdec/haloexchange.cpp on the staged path), so a PP rank's direct MPI partners for halo traffic are its two grid neighbours and nothing else. RETIRED 2026-09-02 as an assertion: the oracle above is right and the QUERY was not, because it resolved a send's peer through ucx_ep_connection -> ucx_worker_address.prefix_hash, the cross-rank join round 1 itself measured as resolving the wrong worker on Open MPI 4.1.x. The same claim is now made by asserts-r2/halo_and_pme_peers_match_the_decomposition.sql, which reads the peer out of the MPI tag and needs no cross-rank join at all. The derivation stays here because it is what that assertion is checked against.
oracle_derivation.pme_coordinate_volume: Every PP rank sends its home atoms' coordinates to its PME rank once per step, and the home-atom counts of the PP ranks partition the system, so the PP->PME coordinate volume per step is natoms * 12 B regardless of how the decomposition moved atoms around. Over nsteps+1 force evaluations that is 12 * natoms * (nsteps+1) bytes. Charges are re-sent on each pair-list/DD rebuild (PP_PME_CHARGE, pme_pp.cpp:212), i.e. nsteps/nstlist + 1 times, adding 4 * natoms * (nsteps/nstlist + 1) bytes.
oracle_derivation.gpudirect: src/gromacs/taskassignment/decidegpuusage.cpp:794 -- direct GPU communication is ON BY DEFAULT in a CUDA + library-MPI build and is turned off only by GMX_DISABLE_DIRECT_GPU_COMM. On the ON path the buffer handed to MPI is a device pointer (gpuhaloexchange_impl_gpu.cpp:489 MPI_Irecv(recvPtr,...)/:492 MPI_Send(sendPtr,...) where both are Float3* into device memory); on the OFF path GROMACS copies to host staging buffers first and MPI only ever sees host memory. So the discriminator in the capture is not the message count and not the byte count -- it is whether the memory the NIC was asked to register is device memory.

not_covered: No gpumem/NVBit pass. The question here is which door the traffic went through, not which byte a kernel touched, and NVBit's module-processing cost (~440 s in case 05) buys nothing for it. No nccl provider: GROMACS 2025.2 links libnvshmem_host but uses NCCL for nothing on this path, and GMX_ENABLE_NVSHMEM is not set.
runner_note: This case does NOT use suite/sql_check.sh. That script materialises `params` from a HARD-CODED column list (PARAM_COLS = ranks nodes gpus iters msg_bytes elems elem_bytes app_buffer_bytes regions_per_rank umem_binding gpudirect rx_depth colls_per_iter p2p_per_iter groups_per_iter) and exits 2 on any workload key outside it, so npp/npme/nsteps/natoms -- the entire oracle of this case -- cannot be stated to it at all. asserts.sh here is the assertion half of sql_check.sh with the column list taken from meta.json instead. See NOTES.md.

expect_fail_asserts.entity_close_accounted: NOT a missing door, and the previous text here was wrong -- it claimed 3,726 closes against openers that were never recorded. Re-measured on job 45103152: every mem-region close names a region that WAS recorded (unmatched = 0). What fires is clause 3, 'entity opened and never closed': 33 of 1,588 ib_mem_region lifetimes are still live at exit, 3-5 per rank evenly across all 8, all origin=1 (the same door as the other 1,508), so they are not a distinct population. That is an application exiting without deregistering, which suite/asserts/entity_close_accounted.sql explicitly calls 'legal and not our problem' and tells you to scope per case rather than exempt -- a global exemption for opener 100 would hide the hcoll leak in BUGS-FOUND.md and the 474 unmatched closes this file was written for. Marked here and nowhere else, exactly as the hcoll case is.
expect_fail_asserts.mem_owner_unambiguous: CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, and the previous text here described the wrong mechanism. It is not that UCX re-registers one base at growing lengths -- that IS a containment chain and the reader already resolves it to the innermost object (nested_refs, not ambiguous_refs; see the co-terminal NCCL case in the assertion). Re-measured on job 45103152: the flagged pairs PARTIALLY OVERLAP by exactly 16 bytes. 0x10a2a480+88016 ends at 0x10a3fc50 while a separate region starts at 0x10a3fc40; 0x112f6830+86288 against 0x1130b930 is the same 16 bytes. Neither contains the other, so no rule picks a winner without inventing one, which is precisely what this assertion exists to say. 198 such rows, and ZERO rows with devices > 1 -- the emitters do not disagree about any device. Nothing to fix in pcomm; the finding is about UCX's registration cache.

probe.why: separates 'UCX never used GPUDirect RDMA' from 'the device registration went through a door -p ib,ucx did not load'. Answer: the former.

input.note: natoms is read from the tpr header (big-endian uint32 at byte 72 = 2136412), not from md.log and not from the capture.

expect_tables_note: ib_post_send is left in expect_tables even though it CANNOT be non-empty on this stack, and it reports [XX] in both arms on purpose. UCX's IB transport has no undefined reference to ibv_post_send at all (nm -D libucp.so.0 / libuct_ib.so.0: zero), so the verbs data plane is structurally unreachable here and comm_edges is empty with it. Silencing that would hide the single biggest coverage gap this case found -- see REPORT.md F1. expect_tables has no xfail mechanism, which is itself worth fixing.
not_covered_note: verbs_is_internode_only reports [skip], not xfail: ib_post_send is empty because UCX has no exported verbs send door at all (the 2026-08-27 door sweep; PLAN-20260815-1540 Future work 1), so the assertion is unanswerable rather than failing. Kept rather than deleted because it becomes answerable the moment the doorbell hijack (PLAN-20260807-1746) lands.
